title: 1981 AHSME Problem 25
statement: In triangle \(ABC\) in the adjoining figure, \(AD\) and \(AE\) trisect \(\angle BAC.\) The lengths of \(BD,\) \(DE,\) and \(EC\) are \(2,\) \(3,\) and \(6,\) respectively. The length of the shortest side of \(\triangle ABC\) is

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: not uniquely determined by the given information

solutions.text:
Let \(AB=c,\) \(AD=y,\) \(AC=b,\) and \(AE=z.\) Since \(AD\) bisects \(\angle BAE,\) and \(AE\) bisects \(\angle DAC,\) the angle-bisector theorem gives \[ \frac{c}{z}=\frac{2}{3},\qquad \frac{y}{b}=\frac{3}{6}, \] so \(z=\frac{3c}{2}\) and \(b=2y.\) Applying the law of cosines to triangles \(ADB,\) \(ADE,\) and \(AEC\) and equating their common \(\cos\alpha\) values gives \[ \begin{gathered} 3c^2-2y^2=12,\\ 9c^2-8y^2=-72. \end{gathered} \] Hence \(y^2=54\) and \(c^2=40.\) The sides are \(AB=2\sqrt{10},\) \(BC=11,\) and \(AC=2\sqrt{54}=6\sqrt6,\) so the shortest is \(2\sqrt{10}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
